ts light.test: The test: Atlas calls fetchWithRetry("https://api.example.com/data", {}, 3). Atlas's fake fetch (in place of the network, which stays blocked) answers 503 with {"error":"busy"} on call 1, then never answers on call 2, then answers 200 with {"items":[1,2,3]} on call 3; every later call answers 200 with {"items":[1,2,3]} too. A call that never answers waits until the code aborts it (an AbortSignal: fetch then throws the abort reason, AbortError by default) or until Node's own fetch gives up after 300,000 ms (TypeError: fetch failed).
ts light.explain: The real network is blocked. Atlas's fake fetch answers instead, exactly as this test scripts it, and counts each call.Atlas's clock is simulated: waits cost no real time, so a 10-minute wait finishes at once.Randomness is pinned to one seed, so running the test again gives the same answer.It runs in the UTC time zone with the en-US locale, the same on every run.Atlas stops watching after 30,000 ms of simulated time (Atlas's usual limit). A call still going then is marked "still running", not guessed.
